newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army kills 40 Hutu rebels.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army kills 40 Hutu rebels.

text.p: Burundi's Tutsi-led army killed more than 40 Hutu rebels in fighting south of the capital Bujumbura, eyewitnesses and a senior military source said on Wednesday.
The dead included former students of Bujumbura university who joined rebel militia after Hutus were violently ejected from the campus in 1995, according to eyewitnesses.
"We counted only 40 bodies but we cannot yet count in the valleys where we think lots of rebels have been killed by bombs and mortars," a senior military source said.
A total of 19 weapons were recovered after the clashes and army morale was high, said the source who declined to be identified.
A Reuters correspondent counted 14 bodies at Kanyosha commune, 20 km (13 miles) south of the capital. Some were partly decomposed and all appeared to have been shot in gun battles.
Local Hutus said they were forced by the army to carry guns and ammunition on foot towards the battle zone.

Burundi's military leader Pierre Buyoya announced earlier this month his government had signed a pre-ceasefire agreement with the main Hutu rebel group, the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), after direct talks in Rome.
Buyoya faces opposition from Tutsis fearful that ceding power to CNDD will compromise their security, as well as from rebels battling the army.
The army earlier signalled it was preparing an offensive after fierce clashes just south of Bujumbura.

"Don't be surprised if (the fighting) continues today (Wednesday)," said Lieutenant-Colonel Longin Minani, a Defence Ministry adviser. "We want all of them destroyed. We want to secure the population."
Hundreds of people fled their homes south of Bujumbura on Tuesday afternoon after heavy clashes between rebels and the army.
Residents in the capital heard gunfire and heavy artillery from the surrounding hills.
Minani said rebels had established themselves at Muhuta, Mutambu and Kanyosha -- three communes south of the capital -- but the army was attacking their training camps.
The rebels had established a "parallel administration" in Kanyosha with their own governor and tax system, Minani said.
Residents fleeing the area bore green receipts stamped CNDD, he said.

More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and a civil war between the army and rebels since October 1993, when the country's first elected Hutu president was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.
